title: The Halting Problem: The Question No Computer Can Answer
question: Can a single, general algorithm ever exist that predicts, for any program and any input, whether that program will finish running or loop forever?
summary: In 1936, Alan Turing proved that no such algorithm can exist—not because we haven't found it yet, but because its existence would generate a logical contradiction. The Halting Problem is computer science's own incompleteness theorem: a hard boundary on what computation can ever know about itself, discovered before the first electronic computer was built.
